$comment: Starling trailing spoken instruction record, v1 (#298).
One record per finalized take: whether the trailing delimiter
grammar fired, the payload (everything before the delimiter) and
the instruction (everything after it), with the delimiter and
instruction spans. The payload is a VIEW: the raw recognition text
is preserved and reconstructs as raw == payload + raw[delimiter_span
[0]:] (the delimiter and instruction are the tail). Spans are
Unicode code-point offsets, explicitly not native UTF-16 ranges.
matched false means no delimiter fired: the payload is the whole
text, the instruction is empty and both spans are null. The
deliberate non-fires (mid-take delimiter, quoted mention, literal
escape, empty instruction) are recorded by fixtures/
spoken-instructions.json, not by extra fields here.
The record carries text the user dictated; it is a processing-time
view, not a permission change: it cannot name a provider, route or
grant (the frozen decision and context-snapshot records own those).
Semantics: tests/spoken_instructions.py; Rust port: apps/desktop-gpui/
crates/processing/src/instructions.rs.
Keyword subset: only keywords the repo's minischema.py fallback
understands are used, so jsonschema and minischema agree.
